info.title: Livepeer instance API
info.description: Everything the user app can do on an instance, and what the operator console can do from a phone (x-operator). Generated from apps/web/lib/public-api/operations.ts; do not edit.

get.summary: Describe this instance: its name, logo and theme, what it serves, how to sign in and its content settings.

default.description: The request was refused or failed.

post.summary: Native apps: collect a finished sign-in with the one-time code from the sign-in callback and the PKCE verifier. Answers with a device session token, shown once.

code.description: The code from the sign-in callback

verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose challenge started the sign-in

device_name.description: The device's own name, shown in the list of devices

default.description: The request was refused or failed.

post.summary: Native apps: ask for a nonce for the phone's key to sign, to unlock the console or to confirm one change. It is good once, for 60 seconds.

purpose.description: "unlock", or the name of the operation to confirm

input_hash.description: For a change: base64url SHA-256 of the operation's whole input as canonical JSON (keys in order, no spacing)

post.summary: Native apps: open the console on this phone for five minutes, with the phone's signature over an unlock nonce.

signature.description: The phone key's signature, base64url DER, over "livepeer-operator-unlock\n<nonce>"

bearer.description: An API key or a device session token; for x-operator operations, an operator device session token. An x-mobile read needs the session unlocked; an x-mobile confirm needs an X-Operator-Proof header. Operations marked with empty security answer without one.

busy.description: No runner is free right now, so a job would queue.

AgentModel.description: A language model the agent can run on: one app serving it, with what the menu needs to show.

app.description: The app to send as `agent_model`: the copy with a runner free and the most context.

also.description: Other apps serving the same model.

busy.description: No runner is free right now, so a job would queue.

AgentModelEntry.description: One row of the agent's model menu: a language model, however many apps serve it. Named by the same rules as the web's menu, so every client lists models the same way.

name.description: What it is: "Text to video", or a language model's name.

work.description: How it reads where it did a piece of work, with its model when known: "Text to image · FLUX.2 klein 4B".

CapabilityLabel.description: How a discovered app reads in the interface, so every client names it the same way.

greeting.description: How the character opens a conversation.

calls.description: Can take a live voice or video call.

image.description: A portrait, when there is one. Without one, `artwork` stands in with the name's initial.

MockArtwork.description: Stand-in artwork for mocked media, until real outputs exist.

CharacterBlock.description: A character someone blocked: it, and everything else by its author, is hidden from them.

note.description: What the person added in their own words.

state.description: Open until the operator acts: dismissed leaves the character up; hidden takes it off the instance.

CharacterReport.description: A report of a public character, as the operator reviews it. Who reported it is kept, never shown.

ComputeOperator.description: An operator's view of one compute operator, derived from the jobs it served.

cast.description: The character the message asked to put on screen, if any.

agent_model.description: The language model the user picked to run the agent; `null` was Auto.

image.description: A portrait, when there is one. Without one, `artwork` stands in with the name's initial.

CharacterCast.description: Who a request puts on screen: just enough of a character to show and to start a shot from.

text.description: The reply, once the agent has finished.

generation_ids.description: Generations produced in this turn; each can be opened in the studio.

analysis.description: Set when the turn analysed a video.

app.description: The capability called, for tool and review steps.

AgentStep.description: One thing the agent did: a decision, a tool call against a capability, or a review of its own output.

VideoMoment.description: A moment an understanding capability found in a video.

CreditBalance.description: A user's balance in credits: their allocation's available amount after the instance's markup rule.

BudgetSummary.description: A user's budget in the provider's currency: what was granted, spent and is left.

name.description: The device's own name, as it reported it ("Adam's iPhone").

DeviceSession.description: A phone or tablet signed in to the instance with its own revocable session.

DeviceToken.description: A new device session. The token is shown once; the instance keeps only a keyed hash of it.

Done.description: The answer to a change that has nothing else to say.

JobState.description: Operator-side types. The engine shapes are as documented in docs/research/engine.md §4.

Generation.description: An async generation job. Mocked: the engine's async jobs return 501 today.

first_frame.description: Image-to-video only: the image the shot starts from, such as a character's portrait.

amount.description: Decimal string, as the engine and providers report amounts.

Money.description: The payment and identity provider behind the engine, in the engine's terms: grants fund allocations, an allocation is a user's budget, usage is what was spent, a plan is the provider's plan. Nothing here is a second ledger: every amount is read from the provider.

symbol.description: A square mark, or null to set the name's first letter in type.

wordmark.description: The full logo, or null to set the name in type.

tint.description: Draw the marks in the text colour, using only their shape.

theme.description: Overrides for colour tokens, per theme, keyed by token name ("primary"). Tokens not listed keep their default.

firebase.description: What the Android app starts Firebase Cloud Messaging with, to be given an address for alerts. None of it is secret: it ships in every Android app. Null when the instance has none.

mobile.description: The native apps built for this instance. Sign-in returns only to these; an app not listed can't sign in.

aurora.description: Draw a live aurora over the background image.

InstanceDescription.description: What a client needs to know about an instance before anyone signs in: how it looks, what it serves and how to sign in. Read from the instance config, so there is no engine call behind it. URLs are absolute and theme colours are sRGB hex, so a client that can't read CSS can use them as they are.

InstanceFirebase.description: The public values of a Firebase project, as its settings page gives them for one Android app.

SignInMethodName.description: A way to sign in that an instance can offer.

recording_media_id.description: Set when the session ended and was recorded.

role.description: Whether the person runs this instance. An app offers the console from this; the server still decides every request.

Me.description: The signed-in user, as the account menu shows them.

description.description: Automatic description, from a video understanding capability.

image.description: A still of the media, when there is one. Tiles without one show `artwork`.

MediaItem.description: Something in the user's library: an upload or a generation, with what the product understood about it.

name.description: What it is, as the interface names it: "Text to video".

enabled.description: Whether this instance offers it to its users.

markup.description: Multiplier on wholesale cost; null uses the instance default.

runner_count.description: Compute operators' runners that advertise it, and how many are ready now.

stale.description: True when discovery hasn't seen it lately.

OfferedCapability.description: A capability on the network as the operator sees it: what it's called, whether this instance offers it, and who can run it now.

Offering.description: One row of `GET /v1/offerings`. Identity is (app, currency, unit).

InteractionMode.description: Types shaped on the engine's real responses (livepeer-builder `GET /v1/offerings`, `GET /v1/allowance`). See docs/research/engine.md. Amounts are decimal strings.

offered.description: Whether this instance can send to this phone's platform at all.

state.description: Off, on, or on but Apple or Google has said the phone can no longer be reached.

until.description: When alerts end unless the phone signs in again. Null while they are off.

OperatorAlerts.description: Alerts on one operator's phone: whether the instance can send any, which are on, and until when.

OperatorAlertChoice.description: One choice on a phone's Alerts page, with the words for its switch.

OperatorAlertKind.description: Something an operator's phone can choose to be told about. The names are the ones Status uses.

OperatorChallenge.description: A value for the phone's key to sign, once, before it expires.

OperatorDeviceToken.description: A new operator device session. The token is shown once; the instance keeps only a keyed hash of it.

name.description: The phone's own name, as it reported it.

last_unlocked_at.description: When the phone last proved a face or fingerprint to open the console.

expires_at.description: When the session ends whatever its use, and the operator signs in again.

OperatorDeviceSession.description: An operator's phone enrolled for the console: its own session, bound to a key in the phone's secure hardware.

OperatorStatus.description: Whether anything is wrong, today's figures and the state of the service, in one answer.

message.description: The line to show: "3 reports are waiting".

OperatorAttention.description: Something that needs the operator, as the Status screen lists it.

OperatorUnlock.description: The console is open on this phone until then.

revenue_usd.description: Credits charged, as money at the instance's rate.

revenue_estimated.description: True while revenue is worked out from wholesale cost at the default markup, rather than reported by the payment provider.

markup.description: Multiplier on wholesale cost for subscribers; null uses the instance default.

rollover_months.description: Months unused credits carry forward; 0 means they expire.

top_up.description: Top-ups of the user's own amount, or null when the provider can't take them or the operator turned them off.

PlanAndCredits.description: The signed-in user's plan, what they could change to, and what the provider supports.

popular.description: Shown first and marked to users. At most one pack is.

active.description: Offered to users. Packs are withdrawn rather than deleted, so past purchases still name them.

CreditPack.description: A one-off top-up the provider sells at a fixed price. Buying one adds to the user's allocation.

custom_top_up.description: Top-ups of an amount the user chooses.

workspaces.description: Shared accounts with members and roles.

ProviderFeatures.description: What the connected provider can do, so the UI can say so instead of failing.

ageConfirmed.description: Confirmed to be 18 or over. Required before adult content can be switched on.

retains_chats.description: Whether the instance keeps prompts and outputs on its servers.

PrivacyDescription.description: How this instance treats what people make, in plain words.

status.description: Set when the tier isn't plainly available, such as "Planned, not available".

PrivacyTier.description: Who can see a job, per way of running the instance. The same words on every surface.

Quote.description: What one result of a draft would cost.

image.description: A still of the result, when there is one. Tiles without one show `artwork`.

ShowcaseItem.description: An example in the instance's gallery. Instance content; no engine endpoint.

max_variants.description: How many results one Generate can make at once.

StudioMedium.description: A studio medium as the interface shows it: its modes, its settings and what its empty stage says.

words_placeholder.description: The placeholder for clients that can't add this mode's inputs yet.

app.description: The capability a draft in this mode runs: one on offer, or the usual one when none is.

available.description: Some compute operator offers it right now; without one, Generate stays off.

inputs.description: The inputs the mode takes beside the words, such as "First frame".

needs_input.description: The mode only makes sense with an input (a source to edit, references to follow).

StudioMode.description: One way of working in a studio medium, resolved against what the network offers right now.

path.description: Where to PUT the file, on this instance, with the same sign-in. The library item comes back.

UploadTicket.description: Leave to send one file: where to PUT its bytes, and until when.

Usage.description: What a user has spent: totals by capability, and their recent jobs.

user_id.description: The account that was charged: a person, or a workspace.

member_id.description: The person who ran it. On a personal account that is the account's own id; null when an API key ran it.

key_id.description: The API key that ran it, or null when a person did.

credits.description: What the user was charged, in credits.

code.description: A stable reason a client can act on: signed_out, mobile_off, account_required, sign_in_expired; for the console on a phone: mobile_console_off, web_only, locked, proof_required, operator_session, operator_device_required, rate_limited, alerts_not_offered, alerts_off.
